correctness.rationale: For the specified forward cycle, the first row is q_j(s)=(1+2 exp(-ds) cos(s-2πj/3))/3. For d≥√3 the negative fractional power is irreducible Metzler, giving strict positivity at t>0. For 0<d<√3 an entry can be negative only on its arc cos(s-2πj/3)<-1/2. The viable arcs, rather than the full overlapping negative-cosine lobes, have cells (2πn/3,2π(n+1)/3) and component (n+2) mod 3. The damped negative cosine has its maximum at γ_n-arctan d; the log peak decreases in d with derivative -(γ_n-arctan d). The strict peak inequality gives the ceiling, correctly excluding a tangency. The first arc starts with equality at s=0 and has positive derivative of the damped negative cosine there. For the last nonpositive time, the largest eligible index with weak peak inequality is floor[(3/(2π))(B(d)-π/3)]; its peak is within O(1) of log(2)/d, which is also an upper bound for the last root. Rescaling gives both asserted constants. At d=0 the row is a permutation at s∈(2π/3)Z and otherwise has exactly one negative entry. Row sum one then gives the norm formula. An independent high-precision solve of H_1(d)=0 gave d=0.228903469804774575 and α_1=2.570230659003062518. Replay: frozen RESULT.md, Proof, with the cell restriction above.
